To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
an individual multivalent HIV-1 TAT protein transduction domain can activate machinery for lateral transport and endocytosis.
the valence of HIV-1 TatP determines its cellular entry and that an individual mTatP can trigger the machinery of lateral transport and endocytosis.

the multivalent HIV-1 transduction domain (HIV-1 Tat protein, TatP) can be visualized by using a single quantum dot (QD) to track the movement of individual HIV-1 Tat proteins, and that each single HIV-1 TatP can induce the cell's machinery to move it toward the cell center, followed by endocytotic entry.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms underlying the cellular uptake of the HIV- 1 Tat protein transducing domain and the molecular information required to improve the transducing efficiency of TatP.
the mechanism of TatP cell penetration.

the development and application of a single-molecule imaging assay for the study of the mechanisms of Tat protein transduction and the design of TatP nanomachines for intracellular delivery of therapeutic cargoes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the valence of mTatP is a key determinant in regulating its entry and trafficking mechanisms in cells.
the multivalent HIV-1 TAT protein transduction domain can activate machinery for lateral transport and endocytosis.
single-molecule tracking of QDs labeled TatP reveals that an individual multivalent HIV-1 protein transduction domain can activate machinery for lateral transport and endocytosis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the valence of the TatP plays an essential role in its cell surface movement and endocytotic entry, but the number of multimeric TatP is not the only determinant of its transduction efficiency.

the multivalent TatP-QDs were used to track the behavior of individual TatP molecules in living cells, and the data obtained from this tracking assay revealed that an individual mTatP molecule can activate machinery for lateral transport, lipid raft-mediated confinement, and endocytosis.
the single quantum dot tracking assay developed in this work is a powerful tool for studying the cellular behavior of multivalent Tat protein transduction domains (TatP).
The main takeaway from our work is that
the multivalent TatP-QDs behave as cargo delivery machines.

the TatP domain of the HIV- 1 Tat protein is capable of initiating and promoting the cell surface movement of nanoparticles and their internalization into the cells, but only when the nanoparticles are multivalent.
single quantum dot tracking is an excellent tool to study the dynamics of TatP and other nanocarriers.
